QuestionStmt.S: If $2\tan^{-1}(\cos x) = \tan^{-1}(2\cosec x)$, then the value of $x$ is

Solution.S:
$$2\tan^{-1}(\cos x) = \tan^{-1}(2\cos x)$$

$$\Rightarrow \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\cos x}{1 - \cos^2 x}\right) = \tan^{-1}(2\cos x) \quad \left[ 2\tan^{-1}x = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1 - x^2}\right) \right]$$

$$\Rightarrow \frac{2\cos x}{\sin^2 x} = 2\cos x$$

$$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sin^2 x} = 1$$

$$\Rightarrow \sin x = \pm 1$$

But from the original equation, $\cos x$ must be positive. Checking $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$: $\cos x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, which satisfies the equation.

$$\Rightarrow x = \frac{\pi}{4}$$
